rows.question: Which valves must be closed to isolate T4750 for maintenance? List them in the order you would close them, explain the order, and say which connections this drawing does not let you isolate.

required.item: the line from SV 104.01 has no isolation valve

rows.answer:
Derived by graph analysis of the drawing
- GlobeValve 47123/C1 (GlobeValve-2) is the first valve on the upstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47123, DN 80) [E2.2, isolation_boundary]
- GlobeValve 47127/C1 (GlobeValve-1) is the first valve on the upstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47127, DN 50) [E2.3, isolation_boundary]
- ButterflyValve 47124/C1 (ButterflyValve-1) is the first valve on the downstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47124, DN 80) [E2.4, isolation_boundary]
- SV 104.01 (SpringLoadedGlobeSafetyValve-1) discharges into the piping around T4750 (Tank-1) with no valve in between (line 47125, DN 50); it does not relieve this region [E2.5, isolation_boundary]

Summary (model wording; the lists above are what was checked)
The isolation boundary for T4750 includes three shut‑off valves: downstream ButterflyValve‑1 on line 47124 (DN 80) (E2.4), upstream GlobeValve‑2 on line 47123 (DN 80) (E2.2), and upstream GlobeValve‑1 on line 47127 (DN 50) (E2.3). Closing them in the order downstream → upstream (ButterflyValve‑1, then GlobeValve‑2, then GlobeValve‑1) isolates the tank while preventing flow from the tank into downstream piping before cutting off upstream supply. The drawing shows a relief device SV 104.01 (SpringLoadedGlobeSafetyValve‑1) discharging into the tank’s region without an intervening valve, so that connection cannot be isolated (E2.5).
